items.title: [GHSA-5wr8-gcqf-gqf3] aiohttp server lacks an initial request/header timeout
items.summary:
Summary 
 The keepalive timeout was not used during the initial portion of a request. 
 Impact 
 An attacker could keep an idle connection open indefinitely before sending any data. 
 Workaround 
 Use a reverse proxy (as recommended for all production deployments) with sensible keepalive limits.

items.title: [GHSA-494j-54xm-rwp3] AIOHTTP: Secure attribute not enforced for shared cookie
items.summary:
Summary 
 The Secure attribute was not being enforced for the shared cookie. 
 Impact 
 It may be possible to send a shared cookie marked Secure through an unencrypted request. 
            Affected Packages  

   
       aiohttp 
       Ecosystem: pip 
       Severity: low 
       Versions: <= 3

items.title: [GHSA-2g87-pp6c-29x5] aiohttp: Multiple instances of excessive or unbounded memory/CPU use
items.summary:

 Multiple cases were found where aiohttp could use excessive or unbounded memory, or excessive CPU consumption on attacker controlled requests.

items.title: [GHSA-9hjg-9r4m-mvj7] Requests vulnerable to .netrc credentials leak via malicious URLs
items.summary:
Impact 
 Due to a URL parsing issue, Requests releases prior to 2.32.4 may leak .netrc credentials to third parties for specific maliciously-crafted URLs. 
 Workarounds 
 For older versions of Requests, use of the .netrc file can be disabled with  trust_env=False  on your Requests Session ( docs ).

items.title: [GHSA-4xw9-cx39-r355] json-web-token library is vulnerable to a JWT algorithm confusion attack
items.summary:
Summary 
 The json-web-token library is vulnerable to a JWT algorithm confusion attack. 
 Details 
 On line 86 of the 'index.js' file, the algorithm to use for verifying the signature of the JWT token is taken from the JWT token, which at that point is still unverified and thus shouldn't be trusted.
